To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HF-ICFs-60 measure has been found to be reliable, valid, and sensitive to changes in the health and functioning of individuals, and can be used for national and global surveillance and monitoring.

the HF-ICFA60 is a reliable, valid and sensitive to change measure that can be used to monitor health and functioning of populations, and the combined use of the HFICFA60 and the WHOQLBREF can be especially helpful in monitoring the implementation of measures to promote healthy lifestyles, healthy diets, and reduce risk factors for non-communicable disease.

the Health and Function ICF-60 measure is a new measure of health and functioning based on the ICF, and that this measure has been tested in a nationally representative Russian sample and shown to have good psychometric properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new measures that are based on the ICF, and which can be used in monitoring the implementation of the WHO Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases 2013–2020, which is aimed to reduce the risk of premature death from non-communicable disease by 25 % by 2025.

the development of new measures for monitoring health and nutrition status of populations and for exploring the relationship between objective measures of health and functioning and subjective measures of quality of life in relation to noncommunicable diseases.

the development of a tool for the assessment of health and quality of life in relation to noncommunicable diseases, and the results of the research have shown that the HF-IC-F60 is a useful measure of health and functioning, and the WHOQoL-BREF is a useful measure for the assessment of quality of life in the Russian population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HF-ICFs can be used in the context of non-communicability diseases to assess health and functioning and to monitor the effectiveness of interventions.

the HF-ICFF-60 is an instrument that has been developed and validated for use with a nationally representative sample of the Russian population and that it has good psychometric properties, and is sensitive to change in the functioning of the Russian adult population over a one-year period.

the HF-ICFA60 measure can be used as a tool to monitor the health and functioning of individuals and populations in relation to health promotion, prevention, early diagnosis and treatment of non-communicative diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HF-ICFs are a promising new tool for the objective assessment of the health and functioning of individuals and populations and the WHOQOLS are a promising new set of measures for the evaluation of the subjective quality of life of individuals and populations.

the use of the HFICF-60 in combination with WHOQOL-Bref could be useful in the development of a global monitoring system for non-communicable disease risk factors and for monitoring of implementation of policies to reduce non-communicable risk factors.
we developed the first ICF-based measure of functioning, health, and quality of life for the Russian population that can be used in the national and global monitoring of non-communicables disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ICF is an important framework for measuring and understanding the impact of health and nutrition on functioning and quality of life.
the HF-ICFs can be used as a new measure to assess change in health and functioning through changes in nutrition, lifestyle, and health.
the HF-ICFs can provide a useful framework for monitoring and surveillance of the implementation of measures to promote health and functioning of populations.
